rows.uncertainty: Abstract only, three sentences, no numbers apart from the 1% strength. It gives no patient or lesion count, no regimen, no assessment method, no degree of repigmentation and no follow-up, so 'success' cannot be graded as partial repigmentation, complete coverage or lasting match; months after final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE (full text needed). Design is [a case report] only by the publisher's section label, two journal pages (238-9). The abstract states there are no universally safe and efficacious treatments for IGH; it does not say how 'success' was judged or whether any treated spot failed to respond. The quoted result sentence contains a typo in the source ('is this' for 'in this'). Full text is sold through the publisher (jddonline.com cart link); not in PMC or Europe PMC.
rows.citation: Asawanonda P, Sutthipong T, Prejawai N. J Drugs Dermatol 2010 Mar;9(3):238-9

quotes.quote: The authors report the success of 1% pimecrolimus cream in inducing repigmentation is this hypomelanotic disorder.
There are no universally safe and efficacious treatments for this condition.
